inspection.Title: 3D Viewer and inspection documents
inspection.Body: Returned items remain visible in Inventory and in the Quarantine assessment list as one physical item. Hover the Inventory row to open its Quarantine entry. Quarantine hover cards show a short status and 3D Viewer instead of stock-planning details. Choose 3D Viewer to open the correct equipment in the licensed 3D Viewer, then Review inspection or Lifecycle for controlled actions. Users without 3D Viewer can open the lifecycle form directly from the tip. Inventory retains its detailed tips. In Quarantine you can also choose Edit and Review inspection. Upload PDF, Word, Excel or scanned-photo proof, or select existing attached reports. Record Pass or Fail, optional notes, applicable passed tests and the named approver. The actual action date and reason are optional. A blank date uses cached verified internet time when available, otherwise the PC clock. A blank reason records the reviewer and selected decision automatically; the history identifies both automatic defaults and their date source. Manually entered values are retained. Evidence, required tests and explicit approval remain required. Submit and explicitly confirm Release to Service or Approve for Scrap. Required inspection, testing and repair checks still apply. A photo supplies evidence but does not record a passed test. If testing is required, complete it and explicitly select Record Test / Certification. The form explains missing prerequisites before confirmation. Rejected submissions keep the form, notes and attachments for correction. Accept, Cancel, Escape and title-bar close return to the owning MIE window; background completion does not interrupt another application you deliberately selected. Scrap approval does not record completed disposal. One Undo reverses the decision while keeping audit evidence. Licensed users can right-click equipment and choose 3D Viewer. 3D Viewer has information and status on the left, with the attached-documents list in the bottom half of the left pane and the Upload button directly below it. Drag the divider downward to reduce this area; it cannot grow above half the pane. Its position is remembered. Right-click an attachment and choose Save as to save the original file to the PC. The right pane is reserved primarily for document and 3D model viewing. Images fit the preview pane on opening. Use the wheel or plus/minus buttons to zoom, drag with the left or middle mouse button to pan, and Fit or double-click to refit. PDF previews load one page at a time; Word and Excel previews show read-only text or tables. Save as preserves the original file. Use the print button to export the displayed 3D Viewer to PDF or Excel, including the current scene and section. PDF contains a static view. Compatible installed desktop Excel can add the original GLB as a native rotatable object on a separate worksheet; the first sheet preserves the displayed section. 3D Viewer is excluded from File Save project as XLSX. Documents remain inside the MIE project through incremental saving, backup and synchronization; identical file bytes are stored once.  Viewer settings are remembered separately for each equipment item and model, including camera, materials, color, textures, lighting and section settings. The section axis and position can be selected before enabling Cut view. Wheel zoom keeps the point under the pointer fixed; left drag orbits and right or middle drag pans in Navigate mode. Automatic rotation is off by default. The viewer uses the Windows-selected Direct3D adapter when hardware rendering is available; its rendering-tier indicator reports capability, not a guarantee for every driver. Frozen meshes and bitmap view-cube labels reduce redraw work; preferences save in background batches. Pallet boards have wood grain and UV coordinates. Choose an original procedural texture or Upload texture to retain a PNG/JPEG image with the item. Select model UV, box, planar, cylindrical or spherical mapping, repeat or mirror wrapping, clamp, U/V repeat and offset, and rotation. The native presets cover familiar material categories and are approximations, not V-Ray material files or the V-Ray renderer. Damage marking offers a reddish Spot brush with size and softness, a white Circle brush with adjustable thickness, and selectable colors. Raise and Lower brushes deform a preview using size, softness and strength; coarse surfaces refine locally within limits. These are visual damage observations, not dimensional engineering or inspection measurements. Original GLB bytes remain unchanged. Viewer Undo/Redo and Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y handle marking, deformation, texture/material changes and Reset model. Damage records save with the item and remain in project history through incremental save, backup and sync. Returning to Inventory clears active decals and deformations and restores original geometry while retaining prior damage checkpoints and selected scene settings. Undo/Redo of the return restores the corresponding damage state. Save damage marks can retry a failed automatic save. Reset model restores original materials and removes active damage and can itself be undone. 3D Viewer exports show the current scene; any native rotatable Excel object retains the original GLB.PN and SN keep their entered suffix zeros, such as -004. View > Normalize displayed PN / SN is off by default and changes presentation only; duplicate checks still compare canonical identifiers. Attached GLB models use the optional viewer pack, downloaded and verified in the background. If GitHub is unreachable, choose Browse pack and select the required pack from this PC. MIE verifies its approved checksum before installation; an incorrect pack cannot replace a working pack. SWIMS-style scene controls include damped orbiting, automatic rotation, Home, a draggable view cube, six camera views, a large-window option, material and color settings, lighting controls and a standard EUR pallet reference. The native WPF scene approximates the WebGL lighting and materials. Cut view starts at the model center and provides X, Y or Z sections. Drag the shaded double arrow in the scene to move the section along its axis, use the position slider or the focused grip arrow keys for fine adjustment, choose Center section to reset, and reverse the retained side. The arrow can be hidden without disabling the section. Sections are calculated in the background without changing the uploaded model; closed cut faces use plain solid fills without hatching, while inner cavities remain open. Open or non-manifold boundaries are left unfilled. Model metalness, roughness, emissive color and studio lights control the reflected highlights. The viewer uses the Windows hardware rendering path where supported by the graphics driver. Viewer settings are remembered per model. Scene backgrounds, floor and pallet colors are adjustable in Theme Studio. Hidden or closed scenes stop their animation timers. The model filename shares the Settings toolbar row to leave more room for the canvas. Paint has its own fixed clipped UV coordinates and appears above the model texture, independent of texture wrapping, repeat or placement. In deformation mode, left click raises a convex area and right click makes a concave dent; middle drag pans. Stroke pauses do not save or refresh the workbook. Changes commit asynchronously on explicit Save, when leaving or closing the viewer, or when saving or closing the project. Failed writes retain the pending scene for retry. The circular CAD-style ground has soft transparent edges, a polished surface, separate contact shadow and optional model reflection. Ground reflection and Ground shadow can be toggled in Settings and are remembered per item. Reflections automatically fall back to the polished floor for software rendering or scenes above 200,000 displayed triangles. Theme Studio Model Floor controls the ground color. Active damage and deformation brushes project a footprint onto the model before clicking. The preview is not saved or recorded in history; clicking or dragging applies a stroke. Pointer mode clears the preview. Spatial surface indexing and cached decals avoid whole-model searches for each mark. A single background deformation worker reuses completed strokes and processes the latest queued work without restarting every stamp. Tutorials use synthetic data and restore your project. Original GLB models are shared by part number and appear in the attachment list of every matching item, including items added later. Only the original model is shared: inspection documents, uploaded textures, damage marks, deformation and scene settings remain specific to the individual item. The original bytes are stored once by content hash; incremental synchronization sends only new resources, not the unchanged model. Returning an item to Inventory clears its active damage while retaining its history and scene settings. Selected-item projects include the shared original without another item’s documents or damage. The header search field sits to the left of Undo. Enter a serial number, part number or description, then press Enter or click Search. Typing does not start a search. Matching items are listed with their tab in a scrollable dropdown below the field; all matches are available. Click a result to collapse the list, open its tab and focus its row. Search runs in the background and superseded searches are canceled. Existing per-tab search tools remain available. Press Ctrl+F in any tab to open a themed search popup for that tab and its currently selected subtab. This also works in detached windows. More options expands case-sensitive, whole-word and regular-expression search. Use Enter or Next to find forward and Shift+Enter or Previous to find backward. Editable worksheets offer Replace and Replace All, also available with Ctrl+H, from View mode or Edit mode. Replacement enables editing when needed and uses background processing. Each changed value retains its old and new values in history, and Undo restores a batch together. Read-only logs, graphs, documents and calculated views remain search-only. Search scrolls to and focuses a match with a temporary themed highlight, which is removed when the popup closes. The table keeps the focused row below the popup, including expanded advanced controls. The header search continues to search across tabs. For a Master cell with one PN and several serials, right-click 3D Viewer to open its shared PN model with All serials selected. Only shared models are listed in this mode; serial documents, inspection actions, painting and deformation stay unavailable. Choose a specific serial in the item selector to load its own evidence and damage and enable the editing tools permitted by your role. Select All serials to return to the shared view. Material and connection settings remain PN-specific. A duplicate warning does not suppress the model badge; uploaded model availability refreshes on existing Master columns in the background.

inspection.Title: Navigate, cut and inspect a model
inspection.Body: Use the mouse wheel to zoom towards the pointer, orbit with the left button in Navigate mode, and pan with middle drag. Home and Reset view fit the model; the view selector offers perspective, orthographic and preset directions. Open large 3D view gives more room. In Settings, select the cut axis even before enabling Cut view. Enable it and drag the double-arrow handle or use the position control to move the plane. Turn Cut view off to restore the full model. Scene lighting, ground, camera and item settings are retained separately from the original asset. Damage brush previews show where a mark will land; deformation raises with the left button and dents with the right. Damage remains tied to the SN and follows the existing return-to-service clearing workflow. Uploads support GLB files up to 120 MB within resource limits. Geometry optimization in the gear menu enables adaptive display levels generated in the background from immutable source geometry. Maximum screen error, reusable derived-cache memory and performance diagnostics are adjustable. Turn Adaptive geometry off to compare original geometry at the same camera position. Cuts, connection editing, mesh selection and damage editing use original detail. Diagnostics show estimated UI frame rate, frame interval, submitted triangles, mesh submissions, process RAM and active levels; WPF does not expose GPU timings or hardware draw-call counters. This is adaptive visualization, not a replacement for the original engineering model. The viewer pack contains its verified native optimizer and can fall back to original geometry if optimization is unavailable.

inspection.Title: 3D marking and inspection notes
inspection.Body: Models that contain stamp-area annotation metadata can show 3D callouts and markers for stamp locations in 3D Viewer. Use Show / hide notes to toggle drawing indicators and added notes. The annotations describe where markings belong and do not engrave PN or SN text into the source mesh. Read the evidence classification: drawing-indicated, related-family or unverified locations have different confidence. An absent annotation does not establish that the equipment has no stamp location. Changes to a shared PN model or its configuration refresh open 3D Viewer, Schematics 3D and wizard scenes in the background while retaining navigation and draft selections where they remain valid. In 3D Viewer, use Add note and click the model, or right-click a surface and choose Add note. Replace the selected Test Note text and choose Done to save or Cancel to close the draft. Marking notes use green spots by default. Inspection notes use blue and support spots or bands. For a band, choose its axis, enter its width in millimetres, and choose External, Internal or Both. Use Cut view to inspect highlights inside a bore. Note color opens the color picker. Right-click a callout or band and choose Change note or Delete note. Drag the arrows at the anchor in the 3D view. Spot notes move in four directions and slowly turn the model left at the right edge and right at the left edge. Surface notes move up or down along their band axis. Show / hide notes controls the 3D callouts and the notes list in the lower-right corner, including drawing indicators. Select a note in the list to turn the model toward it and highlight its anchor. If the active cut hides that anchor, selection reverses the retained side at the current plane. Notes follow the model during orbit. Save to defaults to P/N and shares the note across matching equipment. Open a specific unit and choose its S/N to keep an inspection or damage note with that unit. All serials shows shared P/N notes. The label is readable from both sides, including in right-to-left languages. Adaptive geometry uses lighter meshes for small on-screen markers. The model can still cover the part of a note physically behind it. On alternate models for that P/N, placements use the corresponding position within the model bounds. Check alignment when the geometry differs.

inspection.Title: Manage attachments
inspection.Body:
Select a document or GLB in the 3D Viewer attachment list. Click the Delete button beside Upload, press the Delete key while the list is focused, or right-click the selected entry and choose Delete. Review the filename and confirm, or Cancel to keep it. The three actions use the same confirmation and background transaction.
Removal affects only the selected equipment item. Its original file on disk is not deleted. The original bytes and immutable attachment audit records remain available through history, including evidence used for earlier approvals. If the GLB is shared by PN, other equipment keeps its shared original; removing it from one serial does not delete the model for every serial. Identical file aliases on the selected serial are hidden together by resource hash.
Undo restores the attachment and records the restoration; Redo removes it again. Re-uploading the same file explicitly makes it visible again. Other uploads, serial damage records, equipment condition, stock quantities and source files are unchanged. Stale selections and changed equipment are rejected rather than deleting a different attachment. Removed reports are excluded from the current inspection report picker but their historic approval evidence is retained.
Native saves, incremental saves, project exchanges and synchronization retain attachment visibility alongside existing evidence. Projects with removal records require MIE 1.19.13 or newer; older projects still open. Older applications cannot enforce this visibility and are prevented from opening these newer records. Keeping historical evidence means this action does not guarantee a smaller project file. The tutorial uses synthetic evidence and demonstrates Cancel without touching the user's project.
Right-click an attachment and choose Rename to change its displayed filename for this equipment, keeping the file extension. Press F2 as a shortcut. Save as uses the new name; source files and original audit evidence keep their original names. Duplicate active filenames are rejected.
Choose Replace to select one replacement file and confirm. The previous upload is removed from this equipment’s active list and retained in history. Other equipment keeps its shared model. Existing model damage stays with the original model hash and is not transferred onto different geometry. Replacement and rename each support Undo and Redo. Changes are saved in the project, selected-record exchanges and synchronization. Concurrent filename edits use normal field conflict review. Renamed projects require MIE 1.19.13 or newer. The attachment tutorial demonstrates safe selection and cancellation; no user project is changed.

inspection.Title: Inspection, repair, testing and release
inspection.Body:
Send to Quarantine records the condition and reason while retaining the owned physical item. Inspection and testing are applicable by default. If testing is genuinely not applicable, document the exemption justification when quarantining; this is a recorded declaration, not an automatic engineering assessment. Record Inspection records Pass or Fail with evidence. Failed inspection keeps the item unavailable. A new inspection resets test readiness so an old test is not silently reused.
Send for Repair requires the actual facility location and supporting reference. It sets offsite custody and Repair / Rework, removes it from physically held/available stock and retains ownership. Record Repair Completion records evidence, actual location and whether it remains offsite or is physically returned; it does not automatically release the item. Inspection and applicable test/certification results must then be recorded. A failed test keeps the equipment unavailable.
Release to Service requires a passed inspection, applicable passed test or documented exemption, completed repair where required, named confirmation, evidence and an actual service location. Equipment still offsite must be explicitly recorded as physically returned. BER equipment needs a new assessment before release. Successful release transfers the same identity back to Inventory with serviceable/available state. It cannot bypass the engineering evidence checks by ordinary cell editing. Stock calculations and Outstanding update after the transaction.

inspection.Title: Named approval and supporting evidence
inspection.Body:
Release to Service, Approve for Scrap, Complete Disposal and a disposal reversal require a dedicated explicit confirmation. Enter the approver name and surname, action reason and supporting evidence/reference. Attach inspection reports, test certificates, NCRs or disposal documents as appropriate. The confirmation displays the action, unit, quantity, actual date/location, application user, approver and evidence. Its Confirm action button remains disabled until the explicit confirmation checkbox is selected. Cancel records no approval.
The existing license holder name and license user ID are captured automatically when present. They identify the application user, not verified authorization or a currently authenticated operator. The separately entered approver identity is self-declared. When there is no license identity, the workflow captures the declared name and identity source. Approval records include UTC confirmation and recorded timestamps and an extensible approval context. No new roles, Windows-account restrictions, authentication, licensing rules, KeyGen changes or Superadmin changes are introduced. RBAC is deferred to a future major release without requiring a different historical approval record format.
A document reference is allowed when a file is not attached. Embedded files are content-hashed and travel with native project saves and applicable exchanges; History can save an evidence copy. References are declarations, and the application does not verify that an external report proves the engineering condition. App history is read-only through normal controls and detects inconsistent event hashes; users with external file/system access are not prevented by a claimed tamper-proof signature scheme. Offline approvals remain supported.

inspection.Title: Why obtain a license?
inspection.Body: Free users can start with the basic workspace. A license adds 3D equipment and well views, Well Constructor, technical-document references, planning and metrics. Your licensed role determines which data you can change.

inspection.Title: Request activation and continue learning
inspection.Body: Open Help > License activation. Your saved name and surname are filled in automatically. Choose a contact method to prepare your request, then apply the key you receive. Help > Start tutorial and User guide provide detailed help; Help > Start Tour replays this introduction.

view.Title: Your wellhead systems in MIE
view.Body: These scenes were captured from real project wells. The tour plays recorded images; it does not load or modify your models. Serial numbers are not shown.

view.Title: Cut view and formations
view.Body: Orbit the wellhead to inspect its arrangement. Cut View reveals internal equipment and illustrative formation layers. Detailed controls follow in the user guide.

view.Title: Open a project and find your equipment
view.Body: Use File > Open for a MIE project, or Import for a workbook. Tabs group installed equipment, inventory, orders, schematics and history. Search finds records across locations. Save retains your changes and attachments together.

view.Title: Choose your working location
view.Body: The location selector beside Search filters applicable tabs and the hardware offered in Well Constructor. All shows every location. Search still covers all locations and clears the filter when needed to show a selected result.

view.Title: Edit with confidence
view.Body: Double-click a cell to edit when your role permits. Undo reverses changes. Equipment actions and saved changes appear in history. This introduction never changes your project.
